newsitem.title: UK: ALBERT FISHER SEEN VOLATILE AFTER BID DIES.
newsitem.headline: ALBERT FISHER SEEN VOLATILE AFTER BID DIES.

text.p: Shares in food group Albert Fisher Group Plc shed 6-1/2p to 37p, having hit 35p in early trading on Thursday, as disappointment set in after bid talks ended, dealers and analysts said.
"We are bound to see some volatility in the share price today," said one analyst.

"There will be initial disappointment because they've tarted themselves up to sell themselves to somebody. But now they are going to enhance their equity through a buy-back, remain independent and sell bits off which in itself might make them attractive to another bidder," he said.

The company also said it sees full year results broadly in line with last year and its final dividend is seen unchanged at 1.85p per share. Pre-tax profits were 19.1 million stg in the half year to the end of February 1997 and the group made a loss in 1996/97 of 67.8 million.
